business_problem: SNCF Gares&Connexions needed to understand and optimize safety, passenger flow, energy use, and maintenance across large rail stations, but manual monitoring and disconnected building systems could not simulate or manage those environments in real time.
solution_summary: SNCF Gares&Connexions uses Akila's digital twin platform built on NVIDIA Omniverse, NVIDIA Metropolis, and OpenUSD to operate train stations as live simulated environments instead of isolated facilities. Station sensor feeds, building analytics, and visual data are centralized into a digital twin that can model crowd movement, airflow, solar heating, emergency scenarios, and future refurbishments. Metropolis and partner video analytics help feed live awareness into the twin, while Omniverse and OpenUSD make 4K visualization and scenario playback responsive enough for planners and operators to use routinely. The same environment flags leaks or abnormal energy consumption, supports preventive maintenance, and gives rail staff a place to test changes before touching live stations. That architecture turns rail operations from a reactive workflow into one driven by simulation, real-time analytics, and predictive intervention.

data_flow: Station sensor and visual data flow into Akila's digital twin, Omniverse and OpenUSD synchronize the 3D station models, Metropolis-backed analytics surface live events and trends, and operators use the resulting environment to test scenarios, optimize energy, and trigger maintenance actions.
integration_points: train stations across France and Monaco
business_outcome: SNCF Gares&Connexions reported a 20% reduction in energy consumption, completed 100% of preventive maintenance on time, cut downtime by 50%, and reduced response times by 50% by managing stations through a digital twin instead of isolated manual processes.
